record_metadata.historical_significance: SATNET formed an early satellite-based segment of the emerging Internet and played a central role in demonstrating internetworking between heterogeneous packet networks.

conceptual_background.proposal: A link between the ARPANET and the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) network.
conceptual_background.significance: This proposal provided an early conceptual basis for connecting geographically separate packet-switched networks.

national_physical_laboratory.historical_significance: The NPL network was developed by Donald Davies, identified in the article as one of two independent inventors of the concept of packet switching.

trans_atlantic_connectivity_change.description: By the time funding was approved in 1973, the trans-Atlantic connectivity associated with the NORSAR link had changed.

new_route.satellite_station: Nordic satellite station in Tanum, Sweden

historical_result.event: UCL became connected to the ARPANET
historical_result.significance: The connection formed what the source describes as the first heterogeneous interconnected network in the world.

later_UCL_gateway_role.SRCnet_significance: Forerunner of the UK's JANET network

shared_satellite_concept.concept: Use a satellite's 64 kilobit/second link as a shared medium for multiple satellite earth stations within the satellite beam footprint.
shared_satellite_concept.significance: The proposal provided the conceptual foundation for the packet-satellite network that became SATNET.

implementation.relationship_to_roberts_proposal: Implemented the concept of using a shared satellite link for multiple earth stations.

major_participants.role: International research participant and ARPANET connection point

network_interconnection_problem.problem: Interconnection of the ARPANET with other packet networks.
network_interconnection_problem.difficulty: The differences between the networks made direct interconnection very difficult.

international_network_working_group.name: International Network Working Group
international_network_working_group.formation_context: The INWG was formed in response to the need for interoperable network protocols.

first_transmission_control_program_paper.subject: Transmission Control Program
first_transmission_control_program_paper.historical_significance: The presentation represented an early formal proposal for protocols capable of connecting heterogeneous packet networks.

published_proposal.title: A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication

first_internet_demonstration.description: First Transmission Control Program demonstration linking SATNET, ARPANET, and PRNET.
historical_significance: Demonstrated internetworking across heterogeneous packet networks
Connected satellite, wired packet, and radio-based packet networking environments

first_internet_demonstration.internet_legacy: The work surrounding SATNET played a central role in the creation of the Internet protocol suite.

historical_sequence.event: Larry Roberts proposed a connection between ARPANET and the NPL network.
UCL became connected to ARPANET through the trans-Atlantic/Norwegian satellite-linked infrastructure.
Larry Roberts proposed using a 64 kilobit/second satellite link as a shared medium.
Bob Kahn implemented the shared satellite networking concept, resulting in SATNET.
SATNET participated in the first three-network Transmission Control Program demonstration.

relationship_to_PRNET.relationship: PRNET was one of the heterogeneous networks interconnected with SATNET and ARPANET.

demonstration.role: Participated in the first Transmission Control Program demonstration linking three heterogeneous packet networks.

relationship_to_CYCLADES.relationship: The 1974 Cerf-Kahn packet-network intercommunication proposal incorporated concepts developed by CYCLADES designers.
relationship_to_CYCLADES.significance: The source identifies CYCLADES-related concepts as part of the intellectual development of the internetworking protocol work associated with SATNET.

international_connectivity.international_significance: SATNET provided an early mechanism for connecting research networks across national boundaries using packet satellite technology.

technical_architecture.earth_station_model: Multiple satellite earth stations sharing a satellite beam footprint
technical_architecture.architectural_significance: SATNET provided a real-world environment in which protocols had to operate across networks with substantially different technical characteristics.

early_route: Satellite station in the United Kingdom

phase_1.description: Larry Roberts proposes an ARPANET-to-NPL connection.

phase_2.description: Peter T. Kirstein's UCL research group selected to connect to ARPANET.

phase_3.description: Funding approved and trans-Atlantic satellite connectivity reorganized through Tanum, Sweden.

phase_4.description: Two ARPANET TIPs installed in Norway and connected through satellite links.

phase_5.description: UCL terrestrial connection to Norway becomes operational at 9.6 kilobits/second.

phase_6.description: Larry Roberts proposes shared 64 kilobit/second satellite networking.

phase_7.description: Bob Kahn implements the shared satellite concept, producing SATNET.

phase_8.description: Bob Kahn and Vint Cerf develop the Transmission Control Program concept for heterogeneous network interconnection.

phase_9.description: SATNET becomes part of the first ARPANET/SATNET/PRNET internetworking demonstration.

phase_10.description: SATNET connects research sites in the United States, United Kingdom, Norway, Germany, and Italy.

phase_11.description: Peter Kirstein chairs the International Cooperation Board for packet-satellite research coordination.

phase_12.description: SATNET continues to appear in packet-satellite research and testing, including later technical measurement work.

international_cooperation_board.name: International Cooperation Board
international_cooperation_board.purpose: Coordinate activities to develop packet satellite research.

satellite_networking_model.importance: This architecture enabled international packet networking over satellite infrastructure.

licklider_oral_history.historical_significance: The recollection illustrates the administrative and telecommunications-policy difficulties involved in extending experimental packet networks across national telecommunications infrastructure.

timeline.event: Larry Roberts proposed a link between ARPANET and the National Physical Laboratory network.
Peter T. Kirstein's University College London research group was selected instead of NPL for ARPANET connection.
Funding for the UCL connection was approved.
One ARPANET Terminal Interface Processor was installed in Norway and connected via satellite.
UCL's terrestrial circuit to Norway became operational at 9.6 kilobits/second.
A second ARPANET TIP was installed in Norway and connected via satellite.
UCL became connected to ARPANET, forming what the source describes as the first heterogeneous interconnected network in the world.
Larry Roberts proposed using a 64 kilobit/second satellite link as a shared medium.
Bob Kahn considered interconnection between ARPANET and other networks and began work that resulted in SATNET.
Bob Kahn and Vint Cerf presented their first paper on the Transmission Control Program at an INWG meeting at the University of Sussex.
Cerf and Kahn published their protocol proposal for packet-network intercommunication.
SATNET connected research sites in the United States, United Kingdom, Norway, Germany, and Italy.
First Transmission Control Program demonstration linking SATNET, ARPANET, and PRNET.
Peter T. Kirstein chaired the International Cooperation Board formed by Vint Cerf.
SATNET remained part of packet-satellite research and measurement work.

source_caveats.scope: This record reflects the supplied SATNET article rather than an independently researched reconstruction.

terminology.TCP: The article uses the historical term 'Transmission Control Program'; this record preserves that terminology rather than silently replacing it with later TCP terminology.

historical_claims.first_heterogeneous_network: The article explicitly describes the 1973 UCL/ARPANET connection as the first heterogeneous interconnected network in the world.
historical_claims.first_internet_demonstration: The article describes the November 22, 1977 ARPANET/SATNET/PRNET demonstration as the first Transmission Control Program demonstration.
historical_claims.internet_protocol_suite: The article states that SATNET played a central role in the creation of the Internet protocol suite.

network_scope.countries: The article states that by the late 1970s SATNET connected research sites in the United States, United Kingdom, Norway, Germany, and Italy.
network_scope.specific_site_counts: The article does not provide a complete node-by-node SATNET inventory.

technical_scope.satellite_system_details: The article gives the shared 64 kilobit/second concept but does not provide a complete engineering specification for the satellite system.
technical_scope.routing: The article does not provide a complete SATNET routing algorithm or packet-forwarding specification.
technical_scope.hardware: The article identifies ARPANET TIPs in Norway but does not provide a complete SATNET hardware inventory.

IPv4.address_range: The source states that SATNET was assigned 4.x.x.x/8 but does not provide additional details about historical address utilization.

licklider_recollection.limitation: The military-base destination is not identified in the recollection.

source_caveats.source_boundary: No unsupported claims about exact satellites, launch vehicles, frequencies, cryptographic systems, military missions, or operational lifespan have been added.
